full_judgment:
2. The case of the petitioners, in short is that Mahbubur Rahman Talukdar, father of opposite parties I and 4 claiming to be owner of the suit premises in question filed o c. Suit No. 311 of 079 in the Second Court of Munsif, Bogra for ejectment of one Raisuddin and petitioner No 2 and the said suit was decreed on 20.3.83. Petitioner No. 2 preferred an appeal from the said judgment and decree in the Court of the District Judge, Bogra, being O.0 Appeal No. 36 of 1983 which was also dismissed on 8 9.83. Petitioner No. 2 thereafter moved the revisional application in this Court and obtained Rule being Civil Revision No. 13 of 1984. During the pendency of the said Rule the further proceedings in O.C. Execution Case No. 4 of 1984 started by the decree holder Mahbubur Rahman Talukdar was stayed. The opposite parties Nos. 1 and 4 in this Rule ate the sons of Mahbubur Rahrnan Talukdar and opposite party Nos. 2-3 are associated. The said Mahbubur Rahman Talukdar and his son opposite party No. 1 in order to put the petitioner No. 2 to troubles and to evict him by force from the shop in question made a false G.D. Entry in the Sadar Police Station in Bogra on 2.6.84 and on 3.6.84 said Mahbubur Rahman Talukdar, his sons opposite party Nos, 1 and 4, opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 and about 10/12 other persons knowing fully about the Civil Revision No. 13/84 pending in the High Court Division and the said stay order granted therein, being armed with various weapons attacked petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 illegally trespassing into the said shop and assaulted the petitioner No. 2 who somehow escaped and took shelter in the police station, which is situated at the distance of i.50 yards. One of the Police Officers came to the shop and arrested opposite parties Nos. 1 and 2 asked the petitioner No 2 to go to the police station. After locking up the door of the shop the petitioner No. 2 went to the police station, but the police illegally arrested the petitioner No. 2 in connection with the said G.D. Entry No. 52 dated 2.6.84 and put another lock on the door of the shop of the petitioner, who had already locked the door of the shop. The further case of the petitioner No. 2 is that while he was in hajat his grandfather petitioner No. 1 Alhaj Ralamanuddin Shah lodged F.I.R. in the police station, Bogra, being P.S. Case No. 2 (3)/84 dated 3.6184 giving rise to G.R. Case No. 157 of 1984. 

 4. Mr. Abdul Momin Talukdar, the learned Advocate appearing for petitioners, argued that police illegally put look wad key on the shop of the petitioner No. 2 and prayed for a direction to remove the same in order to enable the petitioner No. 2 to carry on his business. Mr. Abdul Momin Talukdar is quite aware that the rule in Civil Revision No. 13/84 obtained by the petitioner No. 2 herein was discharged by this Court on l6 4 83. thereby the judgment and decree dated 20 3.84 passed by the second Court of Munsif, Sadar Bogra O.C. Suit No. 311/79 has been maintained, and the order staying the Execution Case No. 4 of 1983 arising from the said decree has also been vacated with the disposal of the Rule on 16.4.85. 

 6. It is quite apparent that the petitioners obtained this Rule from this Court without approaching District Magistrate on the Sessions Judge. Therefore, in view of the rule of practice followed in the matter as observed by the appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh the failure of the petitioner to approach the Sessions Judge was a bar to obtaining a Rule from this Court. On this score alone the Rule is liable to be discharged. Mr. Ansar Ali has further submitted that the two petitioners have obtained this Rule against two orders in which they are interested separately. 7. The two orders are of divergent nature and passed in different situations. Civil Revision Case No. 13 of 1984 prefer-red by petitioner No. 2 Matlubor Rahman has already been disposed of upholding the judgment and decree passed in O.C. Suit No. 311/79 for ejectment of the petitioner No. 2 Matlubor Rahman from the shop premises. The stay order granted in the Civil Revision Case has been vacated, and as such the Execution Case No. 4 of 1983 will now proceed for eviction of petitioner No. 2. So, in due process of law the petitioner No. 2 will be ousted from the shop premises, Mr Ansar Ali has submitted that placing a lock and key on the door of the shop in connection with G D Entry No. 52 dated 2.6.84 was intended to prevent petitioner from inducting unauthorised persons in the premises while he himself vacates the same. Mr. Abdul Momin Talukdar undertakes that in the event of removal of the lock by the police his clients will not make any attempt to induct any unauthorised persons in the said shop He will vacate the same in due process of law.
